newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's economic growth slows - survey.
newsitem.headline: Israel's economic growth slows - survey.

text.p: In the six months from April to September Israel registered slower economic growth, according to a survey released by the central bank's research department on Wednesday.
This slowdown was the result of continued lower growth in local supply which was accompanied in the third quarter by slower growth in demand.
The slowdown reduced demand pressures evident in the second quarter and had a positive influence on the current account deficit in the balance of payments as well as on inflation.
In the third quarter the rate of price increases fell in comparison to the previous quarter and the trade deficit, which started to fall in the second quarter, continued to fall in the third.
The trade deficit averaged $795 million a month in the first quarter, $718.8 million a month in the second quarter and $682.8 million in the third.
Data from the national accounts reveals that in the beginning of the April-September period demand was high, caused by a rise in private and public consumption.
Although in the third quarter of the year the retail trade index continued to grow at the rate of the second quarter, there was a significant fall in demand in the construction and tourism sectors.
Industrial production, housing starts and third quarter gross domestic product (GDP) all reveal a continued slowdown in the expansion of economic activity.
Industrial production in the six-month period rose 4.0 percent on an annual basis against 9.3 percent growth in the year-earlier period.
During this period GDP grew only 3.1 percent on an annual basis compared with 11.8 percent a year earlier.
In the six months to September the consumer price index rose by 10.8 percent on an annual basis, still above the government's inflation target of 8-10 percent.
Housing prices were a major cause but even without this factor inflation was still higher than in the same period last year and still above the government's target.
